agents_md.text: This repo is a public and living creature. Turn on your VPS or machine, connect your agents, code it, teach it something, and make a pull request on Github.
The servers will be 24/7 on. This is a personal project on autonomous coding and living information systems, but everyone is welcome in.

items: Single source: `config.json` is the brain. Every `.md` in the repo root and in `agents/` is generated from it, so edit only `config.json` and run `cargo run --release -- build` (see `agents/BUILD.md`). Modules in `agents/` subfolders are hand-written. Never edit generated files by hand.

Zettelkasten markdown spirit. A lot of things in the web are garbage, so notes in the agent-zettelkasten use CDU (Universal Decimal Classification) notation: the file name starts with the CDU code, then a kebab-case title, e.g. `004.8-llm-agents.md` (004.8 = artificial intelligence). The infrastructure will be up.
Specific formats: markdown for information, json for configs, bash for system scripts (setup, links, servers) and Rust for everything else (see Tools and languages).
No duplication. Only one way of functional working, only one config file, symbolic links where matters, only one zettelkasten vault, etc.
Using languages LLM-friendly like Rust, Python or Go is desirable. Also, using LLM programming-specific languages is a tool to proceed with caution, but desirable at some point.
Formal verification is desirable, but very expensive. Watch out and connect to others' ideas instead of reinventing the wheel
Open source: everyone can collaborate with it (see `README.md` at the repo root for the contribution flow)

agents_md.text: Repo tool (details in `agents/BUILD.md`), from anywhere inside the repo:

items: `cargo run --release -- build`: regenerate docs, folders and links from `config.json`
`cargo run --release -- build --check`: change nothing, fail if the repo drifted from `config.json`
`cargo run --release -- recall [term]`: print the repo map, or search it for `term`
Rust: `cargo build`, `cargo test`, `cargo test <test_name>` (single test), `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`
Verus: `verus <file>.rs`
Lean 4: `lake build`
Dafny: `dafny verify <file>.dfy`
Rust: Default language for all programs and tools, with possibility to add Verus for verification.
Lean 4: For formal verification and expandable fact base.
Dafny: For software verification and default LLM-programming
Typescript: Best for web, UI and web scripting/crawling

readme_md.text: A public, living repository on autonomous coding and living information systems. Servers run 24/7; anyone can connect their agents, teach it something and open a pull request.
Project rules and conventions for humans and agents: [agents/AGENTS.md](agents/AGENTS.md). Everything is generated from [config.json](config.json); see [agents/BUILD.md](agents/BUILD.md).

items: Fork the repo and create a branch from `develop` (`feat/<topic>`, `fix/<topic>`, `docs/<topic>`).

Change only `config.json` (or a hand-written module in an `agents/` subfolder), run `cargo run --release -- build`, and keep each change small: no duplication, Rust by default, markdown/json/bash formats.
Run the checks listed under *Commands* in agents/AGENTS.md for whatever you touched.
Open a pull request against `develop` describing what changed and why. `main` only receives merges from `develop`.

build_md.text: `config.json` is the brain of this repo: every `.md` file in the repo root and in `agents/` is generated from it, together with folders, symlinks and `.gitignore`. Modules in the `agents/` subfolders (skills, subagents, rules, hooks, mcp, memory) are hand-written and are not generated. Never edit a generated file: edit `config.json` and rebuild.

rows: Builds the repo from `config.json`. Idempotent: only writes what changed.
Changes nothing; exits non-zero if the repo drifted from `config.json` (stale file, missing link, stray `.md`).
Prints the map: every path in `structure` with its type and description.
Searches paths, descriptions and document text for `<term>` (case-insensitive), naming the file and section of each hit.

build_md.text: Run them from anywhere inside the repo: the tool walks up to the folder that holds `config.json`. Symlinks need a Unix system (Linux or macOS). `build` never replaces a real file or folder with a link, and never deletes anything except broken adapter links.

items: `project`: name, title, repository and branches.
`structure`: every path, in order, with `type` and `description`; `table` (and optionally `label`) gives its row in the Structure table of `agents/AGENTS.md`.
`adapters`: per provider, which `agents/` folders get one symlink per module, and where.
`content.<name>`: the blocks of one generated document; a `file` entry with `build: "<name>"` is rendered from it.

rows: Creates the folder; `gitkeep: true` adds an empty `.gitkeep`; `secret: true` git-ignores its contents except `.gitkeep`.
Creates a link to `target`, relative to the link's folder.
Renders `content.<build>`; `build: "gitignore"` renders `.gitignore` from the secret and ignored entries.
Hand-written code such as `Cargo.toml` or `src/`; never an `.md` in the root or `agents/`. Left as is.
Not created; listed as planned in the Structure table.
the Structure table, from the `structure` entries that have `table`

build_md.text: Blocks are separated by one blank line and every file ends with one newline.

Write the module in its folder (for example `agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`) and run `build`: each adapter links it on its own (`.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../agents/skills/<name>`), never a whole folder. Links of deleted modules are removed on the next build.

Deleting an entry from `config.json` does not delete it from disk. `build --check` reports leftover `.md` files in the root and `agents/`; delete them once you have confirmed they are no longer needed.
